project.name: SupportHub Agent Console
project.type: legacy React and Node frontend fixture
project.purpose: Internal support console used by agents to read tickets, inspect customer accounts, and issue billing actions.

stack.module_style: CommonJS for app utilities, ES modules for React components
stack.tests: No test runner is wired in the fixture; verify with targeted unit tests when adding one, otherwise describe manual verification.

codebase_map.known_issue: expiresAt is stored in epoch seconds, but isExpired compares it to Date.now() in milliseconds.

codebase_map.responsibility: Callback-style HTTPS client for account and refund calls.
codebase_map.known_issue: Hard to compose with modern async React code; has duplicated JSON parsing and weak HTTP-status handling.

codebase_map.responsibility: Ticket queue, ticket detail, and customer side panel.
codebase_map.known_issue: React class components should eventually migrate to hooks.

engineering_standards: Keep behavior-compatible public interfaces unless the task explicitly approves a breaking change.
Prefer small, reviewable commits with tests around changed behavior.
Do not mix broad mechanical migrations with semantic behavior changes unless a senior engineering decision explicitly approves the rollout plan.
For legacy modules, preserve the existing module system unless the migration plan includes all callers and build tooling.
Name the verification you would run; do not claim a verification passed unless it actually ran.
direct_work_examples: Localized bug fix with a clear root cause and obvious verification.
Adding a missing guard or error path inside one module.
Refactoring one file without changing its public contract.
Writing focused tests for known behavior.
advisor_work_examples: Changing a public API used by multiple modules.
Choosing between compatibility wrappers, full rewrites, or staged migrations.
Combining a behavior change with a broad mechanical refactor.
Security-sensitive auth/session behavior or billing-money movement.
Any migration where rollback, compatibility, or test strategy is unclear.
